Let's break down each exercise I mentioned earlier:

* Squats: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, then bend knees and lower body until thighs are parallel to ground. Push back up to starting position.
* Push-ups: Start in plank position with hands shoulder-width apart, lower body until chest nearly touches ground, then push back up.
* Lunges: Step out with one foot, lower body until back knee almost touches ground, then push back up and repeat on other side.
* Planks: Hold body straight from hands to heels for 30-60 seconds.
* Burpees: Start in standing position, drop down into squat, kick feet back into plank, do a push-up, then quickly return to standing.

These exercises work multiple muscle groups and can be modified or progressed as needed.

Here are some additional tips and suggestions:

* Start with shorter sets (10-15 repetitions) and gradually increase as you build endurance.
* Focus on proper form and technique over the number of repetitions.
* Warm up before each workout by marching in place, jumping jacks, or other light movements.
* Cool down afterwards with static stretches for major muscle groups (hamstrings, quadriceps, chest, back).
* Aim to do at least 3-4 sets of exercises per muscle group, with rest days in between.

Some additional exercises you can add to your routine include:

* Mountain climbers: Alternate between squatting position and quickly bringing one knee up towards chest.
* Wall sit: Stand with back against wall, slide down into seated position, hold for 30 seconds to a minute.
* Leg raises: Lie on back, raise one leg towards ceiling, lower it back down without touching the ground.

Remember to listen to your body and rest when needed. If you experience any pain or discomfort, consult a professional for guidance.
